message.content:
Here’s a quick reference to the **federal public holidays that create “long weekends”** in Canada for 2023.  
(If you’re planning trips in a specific province, let me know—there are a few extra provincial holidays that can add more long‑weekend options.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span (inclusive) |
|---------|-------------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| New Year’s Day (observed) | Jan 2 | Mon | Dec 31 – Jan 2 |
| Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, MB, NB, NL, PEI, SK) | Feb 20 | Mon | Feb 18 – Feb 20 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Fri | Apr 5 – Apr 7 |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Mon | May 20 – May 22 |
| Canada Day (observed) | Jul 3 | Mon | Jul 1 – Jul 3 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Mon | Sep 2 – Sep 4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Mon | Oct 7 – Oct 9 |
| Christmas | Dec 25 | Mon | Dec 23 – Dec 25 |

> **Note:**  
> • Some provinces observe *St. Patrick’s Day* (Mar 17) or *St. George’s Day* (Mar 23) as a statutory holiday, which can also create a long weekend if they fall on a Friday or Monday.  
> • *Remembrance Day* (Nov 11) is a statutory holiday in most provinces but does not usually form a long weekend unless you take an extra day off.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the provincial variations or any other details!
